preconditions.description: The number of test cases t must be between 1 and 1000.
The number of vertices n in each test case must be between 3 and 100000.
The sum of all n values across all test cases must not exceed 100000.

postconditions.description: The output permutation p must contain n distinct numbers.
The output permutation q must contain n-2 distinct numbers.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= p[i] <= n for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: All elements in the permutation p must be valid vertex numbers between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= q[i] <= n - 2 for i in range(n - 2))
postconditions.description: All elements in the permutation q must be valid piece indices between 1 and n-2.

candidate_issues.task_evidence: The sum of n for all test cases does not exceed 10^5.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure the output permutations p and q correspond to the correct order of cutting pieces.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: Formally, you have to find two permutations p_1, p_2, ..., p_n and q_1, q_2, ..., q_{n - 2} such that if the cake vertices are numbered with the numbers p_1, p_2, ..., p_n in order clockwise or counterclockwise, then when cutting pieces of the cake in the order q_1, q_2, ..., q_{n - 2} always cuts off a triangular piece so that the remaining part forms one convex polygon.
